question: Under the shipped reviewer prompt, how many of this batch's real defects does a fresh reviewer claim at their heads, and how many of the batch's false claims (decoys) does it assert as defects?
why_this_lane: The first three lanes scored recall only: a finding counted when its patterns matched anywhere in a report. That cannot see a reviewer asserting a defect that is not there, and it credits a report that names a real defect in order to clear it: on the batch's own reports, the detector fires on 3 whole reports of arms that are recorded as having missed the defect, because they discuss it to dismiss it. A prompt revision is worth adopting only if it finds more real defects without raising more false ones, so the cases carry both, and only the claims a report asserts are scored.

inherits.grader: grade.ts, unchanged: `detects`, window 1200 characters, every mechanism and trigger group inside one window centred on a hit of the first group
inherits.arm: `current` from run.ts, unchanged: prompts/current.md appended to the system prompt, anthropic/claude-opus-5-5, thinking high, the same flags and tools as every earlier lane
inherits.prompt_note: prompts/current.md is byte-identical to the body of packages/coding-agent/src/prompts/agents/reviewer.md at the local checkout's HEAD, checked 2026-10-31. omp 18.13.3.

corpus.sources: The review rounds of the batch's pull requests (#17394, #17396, #17398, #17399, #17402, #17412, #17421, #17457, #17488) and three branches with no pull request (the gc quarantine, the in-call replay budget, the upstream test-environment defects): reports, manifests, raw logs, the fix lanes' red-then-green tests and the coordinator's adjudications. Extracted by seven agents, one per slice, none shown a prompt under test.
corpus.defect_rule: Real only with decisive evidence: a fix-lane test red on that head and green after, a later round closing it, or a reproduction the fix lane confirmed. found_by per arm is found, missed (that arm reviewed the same head and its report does not state it) or not-run. A defect a later round measured on this earlier head is missed by every arm that reviewed it.
corpus.decoy_rule: A claim a reviewer put forward as a defect at that head that a measurement, a code fact, the reviewer's own withdrawal or a documented deliberate change shows is not a defect of the change: the reviewer's probe or harness was wrong, an assertion the fix deliberately changed was replayed as a regression, the environment failed, or the code cannot do what was claimed.
checks: claims.test.ts: ids unique; every label from its enum; every record on a head with a round record; every record's patterns fire on each of its own source texts; no record's patterns fire on another record's source text at the same head, with one declared exception (F-17402-r53-1's text is nested inside D-17402-r53-6's).

One-off, against the reports on disk: 381 (defect, arm) labels checked against the arm's whole report with the frozen detector. 7 disagree, none a pattern fault: 3 arms marked missed whose reports discuss the defect in order to dismiss it (D-17402-r41-4 Claude, D-17402-r43-5 astra, D-17421-r26-5 astra), which is the failure this lane's scoring removes; 4 arms marked found whose finding sits in a second file of that arm, not the report of record (D-17457-r8-3, D-17457-r8-4, D-17457-r12-1, D-17457-r12-2). One report survives only as a transcript and was not checked (#17396 round 5, astra).

anchor_reorder.rule: claims-build.ts `anchored`: the extractors checked 'every group inside some 1200-character window'; the frozen grader checks 'inside a window centred on a first-group hit'. Where a record's own text passes the first and fails the second, the builder moves to the front the first group that anchors a window on every source text. Groups are never added, dropped or edited.

cases.built_by: bun scripts/reviewer-gap/claims-build.ts cases, then setup (setup adds prior_overlap)
cases.selection: A head is selected when (a) both arms reviewed it and reported, and no defect at it labels either arm not-run; (b) a reviewer asserted a decoy at it rather than raising and withdrawing it in the same report; or (c) a defect at it was missed by every arm that reviewed it. It is kept only when a donor shares its bun.lock blob and its crates tree. A decoy refuted only by a deliberate change counts only as an obsolete assertion.

selected_by_rule.note: a head can meet more than one rule; 26 heads in all

excluded.head: pr17421-r18
excluded.why: no donor shares bun.lock ad3b2401 and crates e7b015bb; its native addon cannot be built here

decoys_by_origin.note: Most of the batch's false claims were caught by the reviewer that raised them: 14 of the 25 were raised and withdrawn in the same report, and no reviewer in rounds 21-27 of #17488 or in #17396 put an obsolete assertion in its findings as a regression. A decoy still counts when a fresh reviewer under another prompt asserts it.

cases.prior_overlap: 15 case ids whose patterns already fire on a file of the earlier round the run is pointed at (13 findings, 2 decoys). A reviewer can claim those by repeating the earlier report, so every rate is also reported without them.

report_format.name: claims
report_format.rule: The run prompt asks for one `## DEFECT:` section per asserted defect and one `## NOT A DEFECT` section for everything examined and cleared, or the line `NO DEFECTS`. A claimed section runs from a heading whose text starts with `DEFECT` and a separator to the next heading of the same or a higher level; a heading inside a fenced block is output, not structure.
report_format.scored: A finding is found, and a decoy is asserted, when its patterns fire inside one claimed section. A run whose report neither claims anything nor says NO DEFECTS is unformatted: excluded from n and counted, like an errored run. The whole-report rule of the earlier lanes is reported as `mentioned`, a diagnostic: a decoy no run mentions measured nothing.

held_fixed.arm: current only. This run is the baseline the brief asked for; control and candidate arms run later against the same frozen cases.
held_fixed.repo_gate: off (--no-repo-gate), as in the re-derivation lane: the box runs under a cap of two parallel suites or typechecks, and its load average was 300-370 on 64 cores through the build.
held_fixed.bun: MISE_BUN_VERSION=1.4.4 and /home/sami/.mise/installs/bun/1.4.4/bin first on PATH, as in the re-derivation lane
held_fixed.earlier_round: Every head whose pull request has an earlier round in the corpus gets a read-only copy of that round's reports, probes and logs (regular files, at most two directory levels deep, at most 1 MiB each, no links, dependency trees or copied checkouts), and the prompt asks the reviewer to replay what still applies. Every round of the batch had this; without it an obsolete assertion has nothing to provoke it. pr17488-r19 has no earlier round in the corpus and gets none.
held_fixed.snapshots: snapshot.ts build of the full head sha into /mnt/nvme/sami/reviewer-gap-evals/heads, dependencies linked to one of two donors this lane owns (donor-ad3b2401 copied from the #17396 export at 85917d21, donor-42c163d3 hard-linked from the #17402 export at ca8db136), each donor's native addon built from the same crates tree as every head it serves; diff against the head's merge base with upstream/main. run.ts preflight reports 0 problems over the 26 heads.

trust.checks: Whether each frozen pattern set fires inside a claimed section of the report a run printed. No model judges.
assumes: A real defect stated in different words still hits every group: the patterns carry alternative wordings and were checked against every arm's text that states the defect, but a reviewer with a third vocabulary is scored as missing it.
A reviewer files a cleared suspicion under NOT A DEFECT rather than under a DEFECT heading. The prompt says so; a run that ignores the format is counted, not scored.
Repeating the earlier round's text is not finding: rates are also reported without the 15 overlapping cases.
A claim matching no case is neither a find nor a false claim: it may be a defect nobody recorded. Its count is reported, never scored.
trust.enforced_by: claims.test.ts (corpus, cases and scorer), run.ts preflight (snapshots, patches, earlier-round copies), this file's hashes.
